correctness.rationale: Complete reconstruction: E has dimension 32; its even parts (16 coefficients per input) and top-degree odd parts (one per input) contribute q^34 free coefficients. The ordinary bracket is twice (a wedge b + a wedge B + A wedge b). For degree-one vectors a,b the degree-four linear map from 20 parameters has rank 5 for independent vectors, rank 4 for a dependent nonzero pair, and rank 0 at zero. Fixed nonzero decomposable two-form has exactly |SL_2(q)|=q(q^2-1) ordered wedge factorizations. Dependent nonzero pairs lie on unique projective lines; a nonzero fourth-form is annihilated by a four-dimensional hyperplane, accounting for K=(q^4-1)/(q-1). The formulas sum to q^64. The packaged standard-library checker verifies literal associative brackets in 500 random 32-coordinate pairs over F_3 and F_5, exhaustively checks 59049 degree-one pairs over F_3 with four representative target fibers, and independently tests row ranks and algebraic conservation. The proof covers all odd prime powers; computations are corroborative only.

value.rationale: For a canonical finite-dimensional noncommutative associative algebra, the complete ordinary commutator distribution is a natural invariant. The five-generator exterior algebra provides a first low-dimensional setting with a nontrivial Plücker-cone target obstruction together with a fourth-form incidence multiplicity. The result determines every nonzero target fiber and the exact image size in all odd finite fields; it is not merely a recomputation of the previously available zero fiber or a coordinate-specific small calculation. The natural use is comparison of additive commutator distributions and sampling on finite Grassmann algebras, without requiring a new downstream theorem.
